text: Native Californian, Small Business Owner, Involved Resident.

I moved to Coronado 5 years ago after living in San Diego for 20 years and couldn’t be happier. I attend city council meetings, community events, volunteer, and patronize our local businesses. I’m a member of the Mobility Committee, Fourth of July Board, Coronado Rotary Club, Chamber of Commerce, and Island Beer Club. I have a degree in Economics from SDSU and have been a local business owner for over 20 years. These experiences have given me a unique perspective that will help me be the best representative possible.

Fostering a Healthy Business Environment: Collaborating with the Chamber of Commerce, Discover Coronado, Building Owners, and Business Owners while working on No Vacant Storefronts. Increasing Housing Availability: Enforce short-term rental ban, have vacation rentals register with the city, incentivize property owners to rent or sell, discourage properties from sitting empty.
Environmental Sustainability: Work to finally Fix the Sewage Crisis while preparing for increased weather events and a rising sea. A clean environment is the best investment in our future!
Technology Integration: Utilizing advanced AI Systems to streamline city operations. Maintaining Local Control: Protecting our local zoning and limiting additional density.

text: The Navy first brought my family to Coronado in 2007, and we fell in love with this community. We were incredibly fortunate to make this our permanent home.

Prior to moving here, I practiced law full-time, primarily as a city attorney for the City of Norfolk, VA. Having spent years representing Norfolk and its employees, I understand how local government works from the inside out.

I served on the City of Coronado’s Planning and Design Review Commission from 2022-25. Over the years, I have also served on the Coronado School of the Arts Foundation Board, as a member of the Coronado Unified School District’s Guiding Coalition, as manager and buyer for the non-profit (all volunteer) Naval Officer Spouses Club’s Sand Dollar Too shop on Naval Air Station North Island, and as a volunteer for the Coronado Island Film Festival and Motor Cars on MainStreet.

If elected, I will advocate for greater City transparency and prioritizing public safety by pursuing every viable avenue to address the sewage crisis, advancing the replacement of our obsolete infrastructure including our fire stations, and revisiting our e-bike ordinance.

text: I am running for City Council to protect what keeps Coronado exceptional while preparing for tomorrow. It is time for the next generation of Coronado leaders to step up and get involved. The Coronado we love today did not happen by accident; it was built through generations of responsible stewardship and thoughtful leadership.

Like many military families, I expected Coronado to be another duty station when I arrived in 2015. Instead, it became home—a place where neighbors became family and Sunday summer concerts and Fourth of July celebrations became lifelong memories.

I am a small business owner and Naval Aviator, with a B.S. in Economics from the U.S. Naval Academy and an MBA from the Naval Postgraduate School.
Coronado’s history, engaged community, small-town character, and unique military heritage give the community its charm.
My motto: “Keep Coronado the California Exception”

My priorities are a permanent solution to the Tijuana sewage crisis; strong public safety, including e-bike safety; responsible planning, fiscal discipline, and transparency for major infrastructure projects; strengthening regional leadership and the Navy-City partnership; and protecting Coronado’s quality of life.

I respectfully ask for your vote and trust to serve Coronado.
Learn more at: RickyHoytforCoronado.com

text: For nearly 40 years, Coronado has been my home. It is where my late husband and I raised our three children, built lifelong friendships, and dedicated ourselves to serving this extraordinary community. For the past two years, I have been honored to serve as your appointed City Councilmember. I respectfully ask for your vote to earn a full term and continue the important work ahead.

My commitment to Coronado is rooted in decades of public service. As Coronado’s first Arts Administrator and later a Senior Management Analyst in the City Manager’s Office, I worked alongside residents, city employees, businesses, nonprofits, and regional partners to preserve what makes our community special while planning thoughtfully for its future.

As your Councilmember, I have focused on addressing the cross-border sewage crisis, strengthening public safety, investing in infrastructure, supporting local businesses, preserving our historic character, protecting our beaches, and responsibly managing taxpayer dollars.

A graduate of the University of Southern California, I believe in listening first, building consensus, and putting Coronado above politics. I would be honored to earn your vote so we can preserve our history, protect local control, and plan wisely for Coronado’s future.
